title: Code component <-> Figma node map
description: The running record of which code components have a Figma representation, and where. A component ABSENT from this map has no Figma representation yet — that absence is the signal, which is why entries are added when the work is done and never in advance.

components.description: Keyed by the code component name in PascalCase.

icons.description: Optional. Icons are usually one component set with many variants rather than one entry each.

codePath.description: Repo-relative path to the component's contract directory, e.g. packages/contracts/components/Button. Required and non-null for modelled entries under components; icon entries may have no component contract. verify:figma requires <Name>.contract.json when a path is present.

pageId.description: EPHEMERAL. Source-file local; refreshable, never a durable join.

componentKey.description: Publish-time stable key — the DURABLE join. Null until the source file is published as a library. Never rewrite a non-null key from a scan; a changed key means a different component, not a moved one.

assetType.description: `not-modelled` is the sentinel for a component deliberately not built in Figma. Put the reason in `note` — an empty entry reads as unfinished work.

axes.description: Figma variant properties that correspond to the contract's `axes`: TitleCase property, values exactly that axis's values. verify:figma asserts both directions — no axis the contract lacks, and no contract axis missing from a component set. A disagreement means the two surfaces describe different components.

designAxes.description: Figma-only visual-state properties that correspond to no contract axis, typically a State axis kept for review. Content axes and other non-contract variants are divergences, not designAxes. Whether a state has a public input behind it does not matter here: `disabled` does and `hover` does not, and both may appear. Each value, normalized (trimmed, lowercased, whitespace runs to '-'), must be a state the contract declares, one of a state's enumerated `values`, or `default` for the resting state. One axis flattens states the contract keeps independent — a tab can be selected and focused at once — so treat it as a review aid, not a model of the state space. verify:figma asserts all of this.

dependsOn.description: DIRECT dependencies only — components instanced inside this one. Not transitive.
